$comment: Single source of truth for Intent Prover install steps. Keyed tool > interface > os. Placeholders: {marketplace} = owner/repo; {ref} = '#name' when installing a branch/tag (Claude), empty otherwise; {codex_ref} = '@name' (Codex), empty otherwise. A cell is either full (steps, prereqs, verify, update) or a note pointing at another cell (note, see). Copied by the prover site (scripts/sync-install-json.mjs).

prereqs: Claude desktop app installed
Node.js 18 or newer for the npx plugin-install commands below; plugin execution uses the global intent-prover CLI, not Node.
Git installed (git-scm.com)
steps: Open Terminal and run `node -v`. You should see v18 or higher; if not, install Node from nodejs.org first.
In the same window, run `npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest plugin marketplace add {marketplace}{ref}`, then `npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest plugin install intent@intentcomputing`.
Restart the Claude app, then open a Code-tab session on a local folder.
Ask the intent-prover skill to install or migrate the global CLI if needed. Approve the automatic sign-in link, or run intent-prover login directly.
macos.verify: Type `/intent:doctor` in the session, or click + → Plugins to see intent listed.
macos.update: Run `npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest plugin update intent@intentcomputing` in Terminal, then restart the Claude app.

prereqs: Claude Code installed
The global intent-prover CLI on PATH with hooks-v1, requirements-context-v1, reviews-v1 and scan-v1 capabilities; use the intent-prover skill setup reference to check stable version and capabilities.
steps: Open Terminal in your project and run `claude`.
Run `/plugin marketplace add {marketplace}{ref}`.
Run `/plugin install intent@intentcomputing` and choose "Install for you".
Run `/reload-plugins` (or restart Claude Code).
Ask the intent-prover skill to install or migrate the global CLI if needed. Approve the automatic sign-in link, or run intent-prover login directly.
macos.verify: Type `/intent:doctor`: it shows whether this machine is signed in. Or ask Claude to change a function by 3+ lines and look for an `Intent Prover:` note after the turn.
macos.update: Run `claude plugin update intent@intentcomputing` in your shell (or `/plugin` → Installed → Update now), then `/reload-plugins`. To get updates automatically: `/plugin` → Marketplaces → intentcomputing → Enable auto-update (it is off by default for third-party marketplaces).

prereqs: Claude Code extension for VS Code installed
Node.js 18 or newer for the npx plugin-install commands below; plugin execution uses the global intent-prover CLI, not Node.
Git installed (git-scm.com)
steps: Open the integrated terminal in VS Code (Terminal → New Terminal).
Run `npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest plugin marketplace add {marketplace}{ref}`.
Run `npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest plugin install intent@intentcomputing`.
Reload the VS Code window (Command Palette → Developer: Reload Window) and open the Claude Code panel.
Ask the intent-prover skill to install or migrate the global CLI if needed. Approve the automatic sign-in link, or run intent-prover login directly.
macos.verify: In the Claude Code panel, type `/intent:doctor`: it shows whether this machine is signed in. Or ask Claude to change a function by 3+ lines and look for an `Intent Prover:` note after the turn.
macos.update: Run `npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest plugin update intent@intentcomputing` in the integrated terminal, then reload the window. To get updates automatically, type `/plugins` in the Claude Code panel, open the Marketplaces tab, select intentcomputing and choose Enable auto-update (it is off by default for third-party marketplaces).

prereqs: Codex CLI 0.147 or newer
The global intent-prover CLI on PATH with hooks-v1, requirements-context-v1, reviews-v1 and scan-v1 capabilities; use the intent-prover skill setup reference to check stable version and capabilities.
steps: Open Terminal and run `codex plugin marketplace add {marketplace}{codex_ref}`.
Run `codex plugin add intent@intentcomputing`.
Start `codex` and choose "Trust all and continue" when it says the plugin's hooks need review (or trust them in `/hooks`).
Ask the intent-prover skill to install or migrate the global CLI if needed. Approve the automatic sign-in link, or run intent-prover login directly.
macos.verify: Start `codex`, send a prompt, then ask the agent to run the Intent Prover doctor. Or ask it to change a function by 3+ lines: the check note arrives with your next message.
macos.update: Run `codex plugin marketplace upgrade intentcomputing`, then restart `codex`. Codex may ask you to trust the plugin's hooks again after an update.
